title: A crash in the loop's test copy of the app stops leaving an alert over the person's work
goal: About every other day, the copy of the app the loop tests with is killed by a fault inside macOS (not in the app) while it announces a change to accessibility tools, most likely set off by the window switcher the person runs. Each time, a "quit unexpectedly" alert lands over the person's work and stays in front, and every walk after it fails because the app cannot get focus. Stop the fault reaching the app, or stop the alert reaching the person and the walks.
acceptance: The cause is shown with the crash reports, not guessed
A walk run that used to hit it 3 times a week runs a week without one, or the dialog never reaches the person
After a probe crash, deliberate or not, the next walk run does not fail for want of focus: the alert is gone or never shown

log.note: Triage 2026-10-03: this is not only noise in crash-watch. The rotating check at 12:35Z failed 4 walks (an-editing-session-walk among them) only because a crash alert held the front; all 3 that could be re-run pass on their own. So each of these crashes costs the person a dialog over their work and costs the loop a red check and a standing walk task. Moved up to sit right after the focus work. Also worth answering here: a runner that crashes the probe on purpose to prove a fix (three times on 2026-10-03, 08:37-08:57Z) leaves the same dialog up; whatever dismisses or prevents this dialog should cover those too.
owns no walks; the ones it names are examples

Cause, from the reports and the system log: the 7 macos-ax-notify reports (09-25 to 10-02) are all EXC_GUARD INVALID_OPTIONS in _XMIGPostNotification < _AXUIElementPostNotificationWithInfo, seconds after launch, while Ztabby-Debug (the person's window switcher, running 28 days) observes every app. Not stoppable here: Ztabby has no app exclusion list. The ALERT is the harm, and it is shown only when the crashed probe is a regular Dock app: kill -SEGV on an accessory probe (with and without an editor window) logged ReportCrash 'crashed process was NOT user visible' and no alert; on a probe made regular by a video walk (AppCoordinator.openWindow) it logged 'WAS user visible' and a UserNotificationCenter window took the front.

Built Scripts/probe-crash-alert.mjs (+ Scripts/system-alerts.swift, drill Scripts/probe-crash-alert-drill.mjs, 16 checks). It closes the alert only when it went up after the probe's launch (window numbers count up; mark taken at launch), a probe crash is in ReportCrash's log since then ('Formulating fatal 309 report for corpse[pid] Photonz Probe', persisted even when macOS refuses the report with 'Log limit exceeded', which happened during this task), and it is the single new alert. Each crash is spent once. Wired into playtest.sh on a death (before the 10s report wait), probe-app.sh before launch and on --quit, and go-loop between tasks. Proven live while the person was away: video walk crash -> alert up about 1s, then closed, verdict printed; deliberate crash + --quit -> closed; a stand-in CFUserNotification alert put up after a handled crash survived the next walk; with a stand-in up before launch, a probe crash closed nothing and said so. A first version closed the stand-in (crash not spent); fixed and drilled. crash-watch no longer counts or files macos-ax-notify. Deliberate test crashes marked in queue/crash-watch.json. Scripts/test.sh: 11042 tests passed.

Shipped Scripts/probe-crash-alert.mjs (d8a713b0): after a probe crash, the 'quit unexpectedly' alert is closed within about a second by playtest.sh, and also before every probe launch, on --quit and between tasks; any other alert is left alone. Cause shown from the reports and ReportCrash's log: the alert appears only when the probe is a regular Dock app. The macOS fault itself is not stoppable from this repo (Ztabby has no exclusion list), so crash-watch now lists it without filing. Verified live with deliberate kill -SEGV crashes (closed: walk crash, crash + --quit; left alone: a stand-in alert before launch or after a handled crash), a 16-check drill, and Scripts/test.sh (11042 passed).
